label: David Charles Grusch
narrative: Grusch is the hinge of the modern disclosure record: the first person holding a current TS//SCI clearance with CI and lifestyle polygraph and a UAP Task Force billet to state under oath that the United States runs a multi-decade UAP crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering effort concealed from Congress. His resume is documentary, not anecdotal. The House Oversight Committee published his biography: intelligence officer 2009-2023; 21st Operations Group Space Control Intelligence Cell; 3d Space Experimentation Squadron; Chief, Intelligence Integration Division, Space Security and Defense Program 2013-2016; Senior Intelligence Officer at the National Reconnaissance Office 2016-2021 on the Director's briefing staff coordinating the President's Daily Brief; then GS-15 Senior GEOINT Capabilities Requirements Officer at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency from November 2021 to April 2023. He was NRO's representative to the UAP Task Force 2019-2021 and NGA's co-lead for UAP and trans-medium object analysis from late 2021 into 2022. He testified that in 2019 the UAP Task Force Director tasked him to identify every special access program and controlled access program needed to satisfy the Task Force's congressionally mandated mission; that he was then informed in the course of official duties of a multi-decade crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering program; and that he was denied the read-ons when he requested them. That denial - a cleared officer legally tasked to inventory SAPs being refused - is the structural fact this board turns on. He disclosed to the DoD Inspector General in July 2021 and filed a PPD-19 urgent-concern complaint with the Intelligence Community Inspector General on 25 May 2022 through counsel Charles McCullough III, the IC's first Inspector General; ICIG found it credible and urgent in July 2022. DoD's own Prepublication and Security Review cleared his statements for open publication on 4 and 6 April 2023 - the Pentagon's security apparatus signed off on the words the Pentagon's press office later called unsubstantiated. He went public through Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal in The Debrief on 5 June 2023, on NewsNation with Ross Coulthart days later, and under oath before House Oversight on 26 July 2023, where he stated he had interviewed over 40 witnesses over four years, that biologics came with some recoveries and were nonhuman, that he has personal knowledge of people harmed in the concealment effort, and that the programs run on misappropriation of funds and contractor IR&D self-funding. He has since suffered documented reprisal - clearance revocation, denied promotion, loss of medical retirement per Rep. Eli Crane's 24 July 2025 letter to DoD - and the FOIA leak of his 2014 and 2018 emergency-custody police records to The Intercept in August 2023, which he litigated and lost. Since 27 March 2025 he has been Special Advisor to Rep. Eric Burlison and a fixture of the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, appearing at the 9 June 2026 Capitol press conference where he alleged slush funds of billions of dollars per annum and said the government is aware of several kinds of non-human intelligence.

sub: Former NGA/NRO officer; ICIG complainant; the proximate cause of the UAPDA
tierRationale: Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 1 of 1138, score 178). 78 connections, 10 of them custody/funding/programmatic, 10 official denials recorded against it. Axes C2/A3/D3.

timeline.label: Read-on request denied
timeline.text: Grusch testifies he was informed in the course of official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program and was denied the additional read-ons when he requested them. No official account has ever explained the denial or its authority.

timeline.label: Grusch joins UAPTF; tasked to inventory SAPs
timeline.text: As NRO's representative to the UAP Task Force, Grusch is asked by the Task Force Director to identify all special access programs and controlled access programs needed to satisfy the Task Force's congressionally mandated mission. He is, in his sworn words, cleared to literally all relevant compartments.

timeline.label: Grusch becomes NGA co-lead for UAP analysis
timeline.text: Joins NGA as a GS-15 Senior GEOINT Capabilities Requirements Officer and becomes the agency's co-lead for UAP and trans-medium object analysis, reporting to the UAPTF and later to AARO. Reviewing overhead collection of such events is one of his primary tasks.

timeline.label: Grusch leaves federal service
timeline.text: He departs NGA and the government to pursue accountability through public disclosure, his information cutoff date for anything he can attest to from inside.

timeline.label: Non-human biologics, under oath
timeline.text: Answering Mace, Grusch testifies that biologics came with some recoveries and that they were assessed non-human by people with direct knowledge still on the program.

timeline.label: House Oversight hearing
timeline.text: Grusch testifies under oath, thirteen days after the amendment premised on his allegations is filed.

timeline.label: Grusch testifies under oath
timeline.text: House Oversight hearing at which Grusch testifies that the UAP Task Force Director tasked him to inventory relevant SAPs and that the read-ons were refused.

timeline.label: Judicial Watch On Watch interview
timeline.text: Grusch restates to Chris Farrell that elements of the US government thwarted congressional oversight, withheld information from proper executive branch officials, and illegally concealed recovery and reverse-engineering programs.

timeline.label: Grusch joins Task Force members on UAP declassification
timeline.text: David Grusch appears with bipartisan members of the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, arguing agencies continue to resist congressional efforts and that spending has been hidden.

timeline.label: Grusch speaks on the Capitol steps at a Luna press conference
timeline.text: David Grusch tells reporters the government is aware of 'several' kinds of alien life, describing 'a continuum from corporeal bipedal type life to what I would consider as sentient plasmoid life,' and references four different species. It is his most specific public claim about biology.
